title: Introduction: Sri Daya Mata Memorial Service

# Introduction: Sri Daya Mata Memorial Service

## Opening Invocation

**O Divine Mother, Heavenly Father, Friend, Beloved God, Great Gurus of Self-Realization Fellowship and Yogoda Satsanga Society of India—Jesus Christ, Bhagavan Krishna, Mahavatar Babaji, Lahiri Mahasaya, Swami Sri Yukteswar, and our beloved Guru, Sri Sri Paramahansa Yogananda—saints of all religions, we bow to You all.**

*Beloved souls, we welcome you to this sacred memorial service, where we gather in profound love, gratitude, and deep spiritual communion to honor and celebrate the glorious life of our revered Sanghamitta Sri Daya Mata—our beloved Sri Daya Ma.*

For more than fifty-five years as the spiritual head of Self-Realization Fellowship and Yogoda Satsanga Society of India, Daya Ma served as a living channel for the unconditional love of God and our Guru. She was a mother of compassion to all who crossed her path. Her life was an unbroken hymn of love, devotion, and total surrender to the Divine Mother. Though her physical form is no longer with us, her spiritual presence remains a shining beacon, an eternal source of guidance, warmth, and divine strength for every seeker on this path. Let us quiet our minds and open our hearts as we enter into the holy sanctuary of her memory, her teachings, and her immortal legacy.

---

## A Life Consecrated to the Divine

To understand Sri Daya Mata is to understand the absolute power of pure love. Her name, *Daya Mata*, means "Mother of Compassion," and never was a name more perfectly realized. She did not merely preach the teachings of Paramahansa Yogananda; she lived them. She was the very embodiment of his message of divine love, selfless service, and deep daily meditation.

From her very childhood, her soul was tuned to a higher reality. Even before she met the Guru, her heart yearned for a life entirely dedicated to God. She grew up in Salt Lake City, Utah, and from an early age, she felt a profound inner calling to enter a monastic life. In those days, such a path was practically unheard of in the West, yet her soul knew its destiny.

### The Prophetic Meeting in Salt Lake City

In 1931, the momentous turning point of her life occurred. The young Faye Wright—as she was then known—was seventeen years old when Paramahansa Yogananda came to Salt Lake City to deliver a series of lectures. She was suffering from a severe, painful skin ailment that forced her to wear heavy bandages on her face. Her physical condition was so severe that doctors had little hope of a cure, and she had been forced to leave school.

Yet, her physical suffering was but a catalyst to bring her to the feet of the Master.

**Story • The Soul's Recognition**

Story: In 1931, when Sri Daya Mata was only seventeen years old, she attended a lecture series given by Paramahansa Yogananda in Salt Lake City. She was suffering from severe blood poisoning, and her face was heavily bandaged. As she entered the hall, she saw the Master standing on the platform. The moment she beheld his eyes, a profound recognition awoke within her soul. The Master, looking directly at her, later said, "I am looking for those who will give their lives to God." Daya Mata's soul instantly responded, "I am one." During that lecture series, she was miraculously healed by the Guru's blessing, but far greater was the spiritual healing that bound her to his path forever.

Following that miraculous healing, her dedication was absolute. She left her home, her family, and all worldly prospects to enter the newly established ashram of Paramahansa Yogananda at Mount Washington in Los Angeles. She was one of the earliest monastics of the Self-Realization Fellowship, entering the ashram on November 19, 1931.

---

## The Crucible of Master's Training

The training she received under Paramahansaji was intense, rigorous, and unsparing. The Guru saw the immense spiritual potential in this young, pure-hearted disciple. He knew that she would one day bear the heavy mantle of leadership for his worldwide work. Therefore, he spared her no discipline. He taught her to transcend the ego entirely, to find joy in the humblest of duties, and to keep her attention focused single-mindedly on the Divine Mother.

In those early years at Mount Washington, the work was physically demanding and the resources were scarce. The monastics worked long hours, cooking, cleaning, office-keeping, and organizing the growing work of the Master. But through it all, Daya Mata maintained a state of inner prayer and devotion.

**Story • The Test of the Broom and the Mind**

Story: During her early years of training at Mount Washington, Daya Mata was assigned various humble duties, including sweeping and dusting. One day, while she was vigorously sweeping a hallway, she was entirely absorbed in the physical task. Paramahansaji walked past, looked at her, and remarked, "You are sweeping with your whole mind, but where is your mind for God?" He taught her that the true art of activity is to keep the heart constantly anchored in the silent interior perception of the Divine, even while performing the most mundane duties. She never forgot this lesson, and in all her subsequent years of massive administrative responsibility, her mind remained unbrokenly united with the Divine Mother.

This training forged in her an unshakeable inner peace. No matter how chaotic the external world became, her consciousness remained anchored in the sanctuary of God's presence. She became the Master’s trusted secretary, recording his lectures, his personal conversations, and his spiritual instructions. It is largely due to her meticulous care in preserving his words that we have the volumes of his sublime discourse texts and writings today.

---

## "Only Love Can Take My Place"

Following the mahasamadhi (the final conscious exit from the physical body) of Paramahansa Yogananda on March 7, 1952, the SRF/YSS family was plunged into deep grief. The leadership of the work fell first upon the shoulders of the great saint, Rajarsi Janakananda (James J. Lynn), who had been the Master's most highly advanced disciple. However, Rajarsi's health declined rapidly, and he passed away in February 1955.

At the tender age of forty-one, Sri Daya Mata was elected as the third president of Self-Realization Fellowship and Yogoda Satsanga Society of India. The burden of guiding a worldwide organization, containing hundreds of temples, centers, and monastics, was overwhelming. She felt herself to be entirely inadequate for such a massive task, and she wept before the Master, seeking his guidance.

**Story • Only Love Can Take My Place**

Story: Following the passing of Rajarsi Janakananda in 1955, Daya Mata was chosen to lead the worldwide work of Self-Realization Fellowship and Yogoda Satsanga Society of India. Overwhelmed by the magnitude of the responsibility, she knelt before a portrait of the Master at Mount Washington, weeping and asking how she could possibly guide the souls entrusted to her. Suddenly, she heard the sweet, inner voice of Paramahansaji, echoing clearly in her soul: "When I am gone, only love can take my place. Be so filled with love that you see God in all, and you will know what to do." This divine assurance became the cornerstone of her entire presidency.

For more than five decades, Sri Daya Mata lived by that divine mandate. She did not rule with authority or administrative power; she led through the irresistible power of unconditional love. Every devotee who met her felt that they were her only child. She listened to their trials with endless patience, guided them with gentle wisdom, and prayed for them with a devotion that brought comfort and healing to thousands.

---

## Her Legacy of Global Spiritual Unity

Under Sri Daya Mata’s leadership, the work of Self-Realization Fellowship and Yogoda Satsanga Society of India expanded dramatically across the globe. She made several historic pilgrimages to India, the land of her Gurudeva’s birth, where she helped to revitalize and strengthen the work of Yogoda Satsanga Society.

During her travels in India, she met with many of India’s greatest contemporary saints, including Sri Anandamayi Ma, Sri Neem Karoli Baba, and Swami Sivananda. They instantly recognized her spiritual stature. When she met Anandamayi Ma, the great saint of India embraced her warmly and said, "We are of one spirit. There is no difference." These holy encounters served to build a bridge of spiritual unity between East and West, fulfilling the prophetic mission of Paramahansa Yogananda.

Daya Ma’s messages to the devotees always returned to a few essential truths:

1.  **The Priority of Daily Meditation:** "Do not make excuses," she would say. "Meditation is your lifeline. If you have time to eat, if you have time to sleep, you have time to meditate and commune with the Giver of all life."
2.  **Unconditional Love for God:** She urged devotees to love God for Himself alone, not for what He can give. "O Divine Mother, I want nothing but Thee. Let me love Thee above all else."
3.  **Loyalty to the Guru:** She emphasized that the Guru-disciple relationship is eternal and is the key to spiritual liberation. She lived as a disciple first and foremost, always speaking of herself as a humble instrument of her Guru.
4.  **Practical Application of Yoga:** She encouraged seekers to live balanced lives, combining active service with daily scientific Kriya Yoga meditation.

---

## Her Sacred Passing into the Light

On November 30, 2010, at the age of ninety-six, our beloved Sri Daya Mata peacefully entered into the infinite light of the Divine Mother. Her passing was not a moment of defeat, but a glorious victory. She had completed her earthly mission with flawless grace, dignity, and devotion.

In her final years, even when her physical frame was weak, her consciousness remained radiant and clear. She continued to send her love and blessings to the global family of devotees. Her successor, Sri Mrinalini Mata, who also received direct training from Paramahansaji, noted that Daya Ma’s consciousness had become completely unified with the Divine Mother long before her physical departure.

We do not mourn for her, for she is free, resting forever in the ecstatic embrace of her Beloved. Instead, we gather to express our deepest gratitude for her life. Every book she compiled, every temple she dedicated, every letter she answered, and every prayer she offered was a gift of love to us.

### Living Her Legacy

How do we honor her memory? We do so by living the ideals she personified. We honor her by meditatively practicing Kriya Yoga with deep concentration and devotion. We honor her by cultivating a heart that is free of judgment, resentment, and pride, and instead filled with compassion for all living beings.

Let us close this memorial introduction by tuning our hearts to her signature prayer—a prayer she repeated daily and encouraged all of us to make our own:

*"O Divine Mother, make me a clean channel, a pure instrument, through which Thy love, Thy light, and Thy peace may flow to all who are in need. Let me be a smile on Thy face, a word of comfort from Thy lips, and a hand of help to all Thy children. Guide me, protect me, and keep me forever in Thy sacred heart."*

May her blessing rest upon each one of us, guiding our steps back to our true home in God. Jai Guru. Amen.
